text: This is a regular savings account.
This is a high-yield savings account.
Say you've got five hundred dollars set aside in case your car breaks down.
Either account can hold that money.
The difference is how much the bank pays you while it sits there.
That money the bank pays you is called interest.
A regular savings account can pay interest, and a high-yield savings account usually pays more.
So while you're waiting for that surprise repair, the same five hundred dollars could earn you more.
This is a Roth IRA, and this is a 401k.
Both help you invest for retirement.
A Roth IRA is one you open yourself.
You put in money you've already paid taxes on, and you can use it to buy investments.
Later, if you follow the withdrawal rules, you can take out your money and what it earned tax-free.
You choose how much to put in, and it comes straight out of your paycheck.
If your job offers a match, your employer adds some of its own money when you put in yours.
And yes, you can have both a Roth IRA and a 401k.
